critical_finding_summary.headline: Item 3 (Stage 5 symmetry explanation) holds, but the m=5 half of it was verified by THIS REVIEW, not by the Executor's own submitted artifacts.
critical_finding_summary.detail: run_experiment.py's stage5() computes a symmetry check (2 of 6 needed transpositions) ONLY for S4 (m=4); stage5_m5() builds a fresh S5 every trial with no symmetry check and no group-law-match check at all. execution_report.yaml's symmetry_finding/headline_consequence text is nonetheless presented as covering both the m=4 and m=5 measured_split_rates blocks. This review independently supplied both missing checks (the S5 x4<->T bivariate symmetry identity, and the Stage-5 root-set match rate at both m and both p) and both came out fully consistent with the claimed reduction -- so the reported conclusion is correct, but was under-verified at submission time for the m=5 case specifically.
critical_finding_summary.secondary_finding: The Executor's own stated justification for full S4 symmetry ('transpositions generate S_n') checks only 2 transpositions whose graph does not connect variable x2 to the rest, so it does not by itself establish the blanket claim used to support Stage 5's reduction argument -- independently confirmed true by checking all 6 transpositions, but the gap in the stated argument is real.
